title: Per-vertex IGM reformulation: N=2V+2Es instead of N=6F
description:
Surfaced during PATCH-53 perf investigation. The current PATCH-40v2 / PATCH-48 IGM uses a PER-CORNER variable layout (3 corners per face × 2 axes = 6F unknowns). On Hand-30k that is N=180,662; on rocker-arm-20k (the Lyon 2021 reference mesh) N=120,528. Both are well past ojAlgo's 32-bit flat-index overflow at stride 46340, forcing us onto MTJ iterative solvers.

Bench results on Hand-30k (one relaxed solve):
- CG + Jacobi:  1000 iters / 1.5s — DID NOT CONVERGE
- CG + ICC:     1000 iters / 25s  — DID NOT CONVERGE
- CG + SSOR:    diverged (||x||=1.4e14)
- CG + AMG:     1000 iters / 108s — DID NOT CONVERGE
- ojAlgo SparseLu: did not complete in 20+ minutes

Root cause is NOT the preconditioner — it is the formulation. The per-corner layout introduces 6× redundant unknowns per vertex (one per incident face corner) and equalises them only via SOFT seam-weight rows. The matrix has a near-null space whose dimension scales with mesh-vertex count, and CG plateaus there.

Bommes 2013 / Campen 2014 standard formulation:
- Variables are PER VERTEX: (u_v, v_v) for each mesh vertex (2V).
- Vertices on a seam edge are SPLIT into one chart corner per side of every seam crossing through them.
- Per-edge integer translation (j, k) lives only on seam edges (already done in PATCH-52).
- Cross-edge constraint becomes a row directly on the duplicated vertex pair, no soft equality between sibling corners.

Variable count after rewrite:
- Hand-30k:        ~33k unknowns
- Rocker-arm-20k:  ~23k unknowns

Both fit ojAlgo SparseStore (under 46k) → direct sparse LU/Cholesky in pure Java. Expected solve: <1 s per resolve.

Reference mesh: rocker-arm.obj (Lyon 2021 paper), copied to ixdar-app/test/resources/qgp/rocker-arm/. 20,088 faces / 10,044 vertices.
definition-of-done: IgmHessian rewritten with chart-vertex variable layout. AlignedParameterization, SeamlessParameterization, IterativeRounding, LogBarrier updated. All 53 existing qgp tests still green. Rocker-arm-20k bootstrap solve under 5 s wall clock for relaxed solve, under 30 s for full iterative-rounding pipeline.
testing-plan: 1. New unit test BenchmarkIgmSolveTest runs one relaxed solve on rocker-arm-20k, asserts time < 5s and residual < 1e-4. 2. MetrikoBootstrapTest re-enables injectivity check on Hand-30k. 3. AlignedParameterizationTest, SeamlessParameterizationTest, IgmHessianSeamTest still pass on cube/icosphere baselines. 4. Visual: render rocker-arm UV chart via VerifyIgm CLI; expect connected sheets with seam cuts visible, no flipped triangles.
